Title: Two Critical NGINX HTTP/2 Flaws: What to Patch First
Context: Threat intelligence adds context on whether exploit code is public or attacks are underway, so you can rank a flaw like this against everything else on your list
Full Text:
The web server in front of your applications can now be taken over by someone with no login and no help from your own code. Two critical NGINX flaws, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, make that possible when HTTP/2 is on. F5 and the NGINX project released fixes on November 18, 2026.

Our research team published a full advisory on the NGINX HTTP/2 flaws with version tables, mitigations, and hunting guidance.

Check Point WAF SaaS, Not Vulnerable – Our R&D team assessed these critical NGINX vulnerabilities and found that Check Point WAF as a Service (SaaS) is not vulnerable to them. The way the platform is built and configured doesn’t enable the conditions an attacker would need to exploit them. No customer action is required.

What the flaws do

HTTP/2 lets many requests, called streams, share one connection. NGINX tracks how much data it may send on that connection with a flow-control counter. CVE-2026-123007 breaks that accounting: a canceled stream’s refund pushes the counter past its limit, a later check wraps around, and an invalid length becomes an out-of-bounds memory copy.

The bug has been in NGINX since version 1.9.5, so it covers every release since HTTP/2 support arrived in 2015. Researchers ran code on a server that only served static files, with no backend application and no third-party modules.

CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free in connection handling. When NGINX acts as a reverse proxy and runs low on connection slots, it frees a busy connection mid-request and keeps using the memory. It affects NGINX from version 1.19.7.

How CVE-2026-123007 moves from an HTTP/2 session to code execution, with a summary of both flaws

F5 rates both flaws 9.2 on CVSS v4.0. Neither needs authentication. An attacker only has to open an HTTP/2 connection.

Why the front door is key

NGINX typically terminates HTTPS and routes requests to the applications and APIs behind it. One compromised server can expose the traffic, credentials, and secrets for every site it fronts. Failed attempts crash workers, which gives your team a signal to watch.

Researchers also chained a separate, unpatched Linux SCTP flaw to reach root and escape a container. Blocking the SCTP kernel module where you don’t need it closes that path until a kernel fix ships.

Where exploitation stands

A public proof-of-concept exploit exists for CVE-2026-123007, and national CERTs in Japan, Poland, and France issued alerts. As of November 18, 2026, there are no confirmed attacks in the wild, and neither CVE is in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

The public exploit needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic on one connection and an AVX-512 processor, and it likely fails through a proxy. That slows mass attacks. Targeted attacks face a lower bar.

Three common controls will not carry you here. Researchers defeated ASLR by leaking memory first, WAF rules don’t inspect the HTTP/2 control frames involved, and access logs don’t record them.

Key numbers from the advisory, as of November 18, 2026.

Find your NGINX first

A server is exposed when three things are true: it runs an affected version, it accepts HTTP/2, and an attacker can reach it. Affected versions are NGINX Open Source 1.9.5 to 1.30.6 and 1.31.0 to 1.31.8, plus NGINX Plus 37.x before the fixed builds and NGINX Plus R34 to R36, which get no fix.

Check the version and configuration on the server, then confirm from outside whether it offers HTTP/2. If the second command prints ALPN protocol: h2, HTTP/2 is on.

nginx -v; grep -rnwE 'http2' /etc/nginx/

openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -alpn h2 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep ALPN

Don’t close a finding on the version string alone. Linux distributions often backport fixes without changing the version number, and Ubuntu and Red Hat fixes were still pending on November 18. NGINX inside appliances, ingress controllers, and container images isn’t fixed by operating system updates. The retired Kubernetes ingress-nginx project won’t ship a fix for CVE-2026-123633, so plan a move to a maintained controller.

Where NGINX runs beyond a dedicated web server, and what to do in each case

What to do now

Inventory every NGINX instance, including container images, ingress controllers, load balancers, appliances, and origin servers behind your CDN.

Run the external HTTP/2 check on each internet-facing host and put servers that offer HTTP/2 at the top of the list.

Upgrade internet-facing servers to NGINX 1.30.7 or 1.31.9, or NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1 or 37.3.0.1.

Turn off HTTP/2 on listeners that must wait for a fix. gRPC needs HTTP/2 and breaks without it, so patch those services instead.

Restart NGINX after upgrading, because a reload keeps the old binary. Rebuild container images, then rerun the checks to confirm.

Then hunt for signs of earlier attempts: repeated worker crashes in the error log, NGINX workers starting shells or opening new outbound connections, unusually large and long-lived HTTP/2 sessions, and floods of WINDOW_UPDATE or RST_STREAM frames. None of these proves a compromise, and their absence doesn’t prove a server is safe.

The same release fixes three more critical flaws in the DNS resolver, HTTP/3, and the mail proxy. Turning off HTTP/2 doesn’t block them, so upgrading is the complete fix. Internal servers count too, since an attacker with a foothold in your network can use these flaws to move laterally.

What this means for Check Point WAF customers

Check Point R&D has assessed all five critical NGINX vulnerabilities disclosed in November 2026: CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-121810, and CVE-2026-113425.

WAF SaaS and WAF Agent Docker deployments (standalone)

Check Point WAF SaaS is not vulnerable to these five vulnerabilities, and neither are Check Point WAF Agent Docker images deployed with Check Point’s default configurations. In both cases, the configuration doesn’t enable the conditions required for exploitation:

HTTP/2 flaws (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633): HTTP/2 is disabled on the WAF application listeners.

Resolver flaw (CVE-2026-123634): The standard WAF SaaS configuration and the default WAF Agent configuration don’t enable SSI or mirror subrequests.

HTTP/3 flaw (CVE-2026-121810): HTTP/3 and QUIC aren’t enabled.

Mail proxy flaw (CVE-2026-113425): Neither WAF SaaS nor WAF Agent uses NGINX mail proxy functionality.

WAF SaaS customers aren’t exposed to these five vulnerabilities through the assessed deployment configuration, and no customer action is required.

WAF Agent virtual machine deployments (IaaS)

For WAF Agent deployments that use Check Point-provided VM images, the assessment looks at the deployment architecture and the components handling incoming traffic:

Behind a cloud-managed load balancer (default and recommended): Check Point recommends deploying WAF Agent VMs behind cloud-managed Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Follow your cloud provider’s security advisories and remediation guidance for the managed load balancer infrastructure.

Without a load balancer: Check Point WAF Agent blocks all currently observed exploitation attempts associated with these five vulnerabilities, including where the VM is directly exposed. Check Point still recommends upgrading to the latest WAF Agent version available in the Check Point Portal, which incorporates the official NGINX security fixes.

Behind a customer-managed NGINX front end: If you run a separate NGINX reverse proxy in front of your WAF VMs, assess its version and configuration against the published CVEs and apply the relevant security updates where required.

Updated WAF Agent images for Docker and VM deployments

As an additional security measure, Check Point is preparing updated WAF Agent Docker and VM images based on NGINX version 1.30.7, with the latest official security fixes. Once the updated images are released:

Automatic upgrade enabled: You’ll receive the NGINX security update through the automatic upgrade process, with no manual intervention.

Automatic upgrade disabled: You must upgrade to the latest Check Point WAF Agent version as soon as it’s available.

Check Point strongly recommends keeping automatic upgrades enabled, so security fixes and product updates are deployed on time. You can upgrade your WAF Agent to the latest available version through the Check Point Portal. For details, see the WAF Agent upgrade instructions.

Check Point continues to monitor emerging security vulnerabilities and validate its protection capabilities to maintain the security and resilience of its WAF SaaS platform.

Closing the gap between advisory and action

An advisory gives you a list of affected versions. Your team still has to find where those versions run, which ones an attacker can reach, and which to fix first. That work takes time when NGINX sits in appliances, containers, and servers that nobody has looked at in years.

Exposure management shortens that path. Check Point Exposure Management brings together asset discovery, attack surface management, threat intelligence, prioritization, validation, and remediation guidance in one workflow. It shows where affected software runs across your internet-facing and internal assets, including servers outside your inventory.

Threat intelligence adds context on whether exploit code is public or attacks are underway, so you can rank a flaw like this against everything else on your list. Validation confirms whether an exposure is exploitable in your environment. Remediation guidance then helps your team fix issues in order of risk, with 160+ integrations and a 20-minute agentless setup.

CVE-2026-90817 (CVSS score of 9.8) Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability

The first vulnerability, CVE-2024-10441 (CVSS score 9.8), affects Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) and is caused by improper encoding or escaping of output. Synology has confirmed that attackers are exploiting the flaw in ransomware attacks targeting network-attached storage (NAS) devices. The intrusions have resulted in the deployment of C3RB3R ransomware, putting data stored on vulnerable devices at risk.

The second flaw, CVE-2026-40217 (CVSS score 8.8), affects BerriAI LiteLLM and is classified as an unprotected alternate channel vulnerability. Google Threat Intelligence Group reported that attackers have exploited it to escalate limited-access inference keys into full administrative credentials. They then established persistence to conduct LLMjacking attacks, abusing compromised AI infrastructure to access large language models. The campaigns targeted organizations in the financial services, retail, transportation and technology sectors across North America, South America and the Asia-Pacific region.

The third vulnerability, CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS score 9.8), affects Apache Axis 1.x and involves unsafe reflection. The flaw can allow remote code execution in Atlassian Confluence Data Center when the Remote API feature is enabled. Rapid7 detected attackers exploiting it in a customer environment on November 13, 2026. The threat actors executed shell commands and downloaded scripts through temporary Pinggy and Cloudflare Tunnel domains. They then searched the compromised systems for sensitive information, including credentials, tokens, VPN configurations and private keys. The attackers also queried internal services and attempted to obtain additional credentials. Although some of these attempts failed, they managed to acquire a service account credential and access a production cloud data warehouse. They later used the account to sign in to Microsoft 365. Apache Axis 1.x has reached end of life, and no official fix is available for this branch. Organizations should migrate to an alternative SOAP framework or apply the available community patch.

The fourth vulnerability, CVE-2026-90817 (CVSS score 9.8), affects Vanderbilt University’s Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) platform and is classified as a code injection flaw. Attackers can exploit it through specially crafted HTTP requests that reach an unintended controller route and manipulate file paths or streams during data import operations. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash. Safe Security observed an unknown threat actor exploiting the vulnerability to deploy a temporary web shell, followed by an in-memory loader that retrieved the XMRig cryptocurrency miner. The attackers disguised the miner as image files and the legitimate syslog-ng process, then established persistence through scheduled tasks and an additional SSH key.

CISA has set remediation deadlines for federal agencies, requiring them to address the Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap vulnerabilities by November 21 or December 2, 2026, depending on the flaw. The active exploitation reports underline the need for organizations to identify exposed systems, apply available fixes or mitigations, and investigate possible signs of compromise.

According to Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 22-01: Reducing the Significant Risk of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities, FCEB agencies have to address the identified vulnerabilities by the due date to protect their networks against attacks exploiting the flaws in the catalog.

Experts also recommend that private organizations review the Catalog and address the vulnerabilities in their infrastructure.

Title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
Context: Depthfirst, a security company, says it found the flaw and reported it to the maintainers
Full Text:
PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server.

Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell.

The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 and rated 9.2 out of 10 on the CVSS 4.0 scale by PHP's maintainers. Depthfirst, a security company, says it found the flaw and reported it to the maintainers.

The October 21 PHP releases, which fixed two critical flaws known as PHP2Shell, do not contain this fix. Servers updated then remain affected until they install today's releases. Neither the maintainers nor the company reports any attacks using phpAfterShell.

Who Is Affected and What to Do

These releases are affected, according to the maintainers' security advisory:

Branch

Affected releases

Fixed release

PHP 8.2

Before 8.2.36

8.2.36

PHP 8.3

Before 8.3.37

8.3.37

PHP 8.4

Before 8.4.28

8.4.28

PHP 8.5

Before 8.5.13

8.5.13

PHP 8.6.0, also released today, includes the fix.

The flaw is in the files session handler, which PHP uses by default. Sessions kept in Redis, a database, or another store are outside this defect, though each store's handling of a cut-off update needs its own check.

Whether an attacker needs to log in depends on how the app exposes its session handling.

On the path the company tested, the attacker uses upload progress, a PHP feature that records the progress of a file upload in the user's session. Where the feature is on, a multipart form upload that carries its field makes PHP write to the session before the app's own code runs. The app does not need an upload page, only any page that opens the session later.

PHP 8.1 and older are end-of-life. The official end-of-life mitigation branches for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1 are not affected, but older unpatched builds of those versions are, according to the company.

The company's remediation guidance sets out these steps:

Install the fixed release for your branch, as listed above. If you run PHP 8.1 or older, move to a supported branch.

Rebuild any container images and redeploy.

Check that the PHP version serving web requests is the new one.

If you cannot update yet and your app does not use upload progress, set session.upload_progress.enabled = 0 in php.ini or the server's PHP settings, then restart the PHP workers. Also limit the untrusted data your app stores in sessions.

Switching the feature off is not a full fix. It closes the upload path, but apps that put attacker-controlled data into sessions in other ways remain affected, the maintainers say.

The maintainers listed the same setting on October 21 as a temporary measure for one of the PHP2Shell flaws. Servers that have kept it off since then still need the update.

Moving sessions to a store that replaces records in one step also avoids this defect. The update is still the recommended fix for sites that keep the files handler.

Linux distribution packages may include the fix without changing the PHP version number, according to the company, so the version number alone may not indicate whether a server is fixed.

Once installed, the fixed releases empty the session file before each write and stop the write if that step fails. A cut-off write can still lose session data, but it can no longer leave old data behind for an attacker to use.

The updates also switch upload progress off by default. The Hacker News compared PHP's source code for the October 21 releases and today's. The built-in setting is on in 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12, and off in 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13 and 8.6.0.

The release notes do not mention or explain the change. The sample php.ini files still show the old setting in a commented-out line. A php.ini file, distribution package, or hosting panel that switches the setting on will keep it on.

Where nothing else sets it, apps that rely on upload progress will need it switched back on after the update.

The same releases also fix other PHP security flaws.

How the Attack Works

The attack starts with the session write that upload progress makes before the app's code runs, Depthfirst's researchers say in their technical analysis.

A PHP session file stores each value as a name followed by serialized data. Length fields in that data tell PHP where each string ends, and nothing in the file marks a write as finished.

PHP locks the file while it writes, but the lock cannot undo a write that stops halfway. If the worker process dies partway through, the file can retain the start of the new data and the end of the old data.

By setting the lengths in the new data, an attacker can make text that sat harmlessly inside the old data read as a separate record, including a serialized object. The next request that calls session_start() loads that record and creates the object.

The researchers' public proof uses a harmless built-in object, stdClass, which appears in the session once the file is mixed.

The emergency PHP2Shell fixes on October 21 addressed an earlier attack via the same step.

"The original exploit stopped working, but the underlying problem was still there," the researchers say of the PHP2Shell patch.

That exploit needed objects to become active while PHP recorded upload progress, so the maintainers limited which classes can load at that moment. The change did not touch the file write. The object data still reaches the disk and becomes active later, when an ordinary request calls session_start().

The attack depends on stopping the write at the right moment. The maintainers say one way is a hard memory-limit failure in another thread of a threaded PHP build, which can kill the process mid-write.

Code execution then still needs a suitable gadget chain in the app, and the flaw can also corrupt session state.

In the researchers' own Linux tests, PHP's execution timeout fired only after the write had finished, so they used an out-of-memory kill to stop the worker mid-write instead.

The planted object appeared on the 11th attempt in a fresh run. That count measures getting the file into the right state on their servers, not how often code execution succeeds.

Their own chain needed no gadget from the app, the researchers say. It used a second bug instead, memory corruption in one of PHP's built-in classes.

They are holding back its details for coordinated disclosure and have not said whether that bug is fixed in today's releases.

The same trick can also replace ordinary session values, such as who is logged in, their permissions, or a CSRF token, before the app checks them, the researchers say.

Title: 'November2Shell' Continues with 7 Patched Ruby Vulnerabilities
Context: Ruby2Shell highlights a familiar challenge in vulnerability response: knowing a fix is available doesn’t mean the risk is resolved
Full Text:
TL;DR

Ruby fixed seven vulnerabilities in string case conversion and regular expression handling, with proof-of-concept exploits showing that some can lead to remote code execution.

Organizations should upgrade to Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13, or 4.0.10 and check vendor updates for Ruby bundled with applications or container images.

Ruby has released security updates for seven vulnerabilities in its string case-conversion and regular-expression code. One of the flaws, known as Ruby2Shell (CVE-2026-132825), can cause a heap buffer overflow when Ruby changes the case of a crafted string. The other vulnerabilities affect regular-expression compilation, matching, and conversion.

Ruby’s security team says proof-of-concept exploits show that some of these issues can lead to remote code execution in certain scenarios. However, the risk depends on how an application uses Ruby, for example, whether it processes attacker-controlled strings or regular-expression patterns.

How Ruby Applications Are Impacted

Ruby is a programming language used to build web applications, automation tools, and other software. It powers popular frameworks such as Ruby on Rails and is also included in self-hosted platforms and developer tools, so a vulnerability in Ruby itself can affect many kinds of applications.

Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0-3.4.12, and 4.0.0-4.0.9 are all impacted by these vulnerabilities. The exact risk depends on how the application processes that input, but Ruby warns that some of the flaws can enable remote code execution in certain scenarios. The table below summarizes the advisories and potential impact.

Vulnerability

Overview

CVE-2026-132825 (Ruby2Shell)

Changing the case of a crafted string can cause a one-byte heap buffer overflow, potentially leading to remote code execution in some scenarios.

Sonatype-2026-012807(CVE requested, not yet assigned at publication)

Compiling a crafted regular-expression pattern can trigger a double free, potentially leading to remote code execution when an application compiles attacker-controlled patterns.

Sonatype-2026-012808(CVE requested, not yet assigned at publication)

Case conversion can trigger an integer overflow and heap buffer overflow. Changing the case of a crafted string may lead to remote code execution.

Sonatype-2026-012809(CVE requested, not yet assigned at publication)

Matching against a crafted regular-expression pattern can cause an out-of-bounds read. Ruby reports that this flaw may lead to attacker-controlled memory corruption in some scenarios.

Sonatype-2026-012810(CVE requested, not yet assigned at publication)

Compiling a crafted regular-expression pattern can trigger an integer overflow and heap buffer overflow, potentially leading to remote code execution in applications that compile attacker-controlled patterns.

Sonatype-2026-012811(CVE requested, not yet assigned at publication)

Converting a crafted regular expression with Regexp#to_s can cause a heap buffer overflow, potentially exposing information or enabling remote code execution in some scenarios.

Sonatype-2026-012812(CVE requested, not yet assigned at publication)

Matching a crafted string with a case-insensitive backreference can cause an out-of-bounds read, potentially disclosing memory contents or crashing the process.

What Companies Should Do Now

Treat these Ruby vulnerabilities as an urgent patching issue, and organizations should upgrade to a fixed version as soon as possible. Sonatype’s Security Event on these vulnerabilities tracks current guidance and response recommendations.

Ruby2Shell highlights a familiar challenge in vulnerability response: knowing a fix is available doesn’t mean the risk is resolved. Organizations need to find every affected Ruby runtime, identify who owns the update, and make sure the patched release reaches production, including Ruby bundled in products and services.

Organizations should:

Inventory systems running Ruby. Check production servers, containers, build images, serverless environments, and self-hosted products that bundle Ruby. Confirm the version actually running in production and not just the version listed in the development file.

Prioritize patching Rails and classic-style Sinatra applications first.

Update to 4.0.10, 3.4.13, or 3.3.14. Rebuild images and restart application processes so the fix is active.

If you are currently using Ruby 3.2 or earlier, it is end of life (EOL) and no fixes are available. Move all workloads to a supported version of Ruby.

For ongoing details and links to current advisories, see the official Ruby security advisory.

Title: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs
Context: The PHP dev team released security updates for 18 vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on vulnerable...
Full Text:
The PHP dev team released security updates for 18 vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on vulnerable servers.

The updates were released Thursday, November 19, for all supported PHP branches, with PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36 now available.

Security firm Aikido reports that the updates address 18 CVEs affecting PHP's core engine, session handling, PHP-FPM, CGI, and other components.

One of the most serious flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-129289, is a critical PHP-FPM request smuggling vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.2.

According to Aikido, the flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute PHP code remotely on vulnerable servers that reuse connections to PHP-FPM under certain conditions.

The vulnerability affects certain nginx, Apache, HAProxy, and LSAPI configurations that reuse backend connections to PHP-FPM.

Standard nginx and Apache configurations that do not reuse backend connections are not affected by the attack.

Other important vulnerabilities fixed in the updates include:

CVE-2026-129474: A use-after-free vulnerability involving magic method backtraces that could lead to remote code execution.

CVE-2026-129496: A timezone cache use-after-free vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.

CVE-2026-126714: A vulnerability involving partially overwritten session files that could lead to remote code execution.

CVE-2026-115560: A session serializer mismatch vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.

CVE-2026-129291: A PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free vulnerability that could lead to local privilege escalation.

CVE-2026-128090: A PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass vulnerability involving an algorithm downgrade.

Additional fixes address memory corruption, information disclosure, cross-site scripting, denial-of-service issues, and potentially unsafe handling of HTTPS and FTPS URLs.

The releases follow a warning issued Wednesday by the PHP security team that the upcoming updates would address vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions, with the highest severity rated critical.

"The issues rated CRITICAL require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups," the PHP security team warned.

One of the vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-115560, was already disclosed in an October 23 informational advisory and relates to how PHP handles session data under certain configurations, potentially leading to remote code execution.

As a temporary mitigation, PHP recommended disabling session upload progress by setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restarting PHP workers. This setting was also recommended to mitigate the recent PHP2Shell flaws.

For CVE-2026-129289, administrators who cannot immediately install the security updates can mitigate the vulnerability by disabling persistent backend connections between their web servers and PHP-FPM, ensuring connections are closed after each request.

Aikido warns that these mitigations do not address all vulnerabilities fixed in the November updates and recommends ensuring PHP-FPM and LSAPI listeners are not directly exposed to untrusted networks.

Although the official security updates are limited to supported PHP branches, third-party maintainer Ondrej Surý has also released patched packages for unsupported PHP versions dating back to PHP 5.6.

Aikido has similarly released hardened PHP container images containing backported security fixes for unsupported versions, including PHP 5.6, 7.0, 7.1, 7.2, 7.4, and 8.1.

PHP administrators are urged to upgrade to PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, or 8.2.36, depending on their supported branch, to address the newly disclosed vulnerabilities.

Title: PHP Patches 7 Critical Flaws, Including Session and PHP-FPM Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-115560, CVE-2026-129289)
Context: 0 (released with the fixes) These ranges apply to CVE-2026-115560, CVE-2026-129289 and most of the other vulnerabilities in the release; a few affect only some branches (see below)
Full Text:
On November 19, 2026, the PHP project released PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13, fixing 17 vulnerabilities. Seven are rated critical by the PHP project (CVSS 4.0 9.2), including CVE-2026-115560, a session serializer mismatch that can lead to remote code execution, and CVE-2026-129289, a PHP-FPM request smuggling flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker forge a backend request and execute attacker-controlled PHP code. PHP 8.6.0, released the same day, already includes the fixes.

PHP runs a large share of the world’s websites and web applications, in virtual machines, containers and managed platforms alike. CVE-2026-115560 was pre-announced in October, a few days after the PHP2Shell fixes (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), with the mitigation of disabling session upload progress. Today’s release publishes its full details and fixes it alongside 16 other vulnerabilities. Several of them need specific configurations, but the release as a whole affects every supported PHP branch.

PHP November 2026 security release: key facts

Fact

Detail

CVEs

17 in total; critical: CVE-2026-115560, CVE-2026-129289, CVE-2026-126714, CVE-2026-129496, CVE-2026-129481, CVE-2026-129474, CVE-2026-129182

Type

Deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502) in the session extension; HTTP request smuggling (CWE-444) in PHP-FPM; several use-after-free bugs

Severity

Rated critical by the PHP project (CVSS 4.0 9.2) for all seven; NVD score pending

Required configuration

CVE-2026-115560: session upload progress enabled and mismatched session serializers. CVE-2026-129289: PHP-FPM behind a front end that reuses FastCGI connections

Affected versions

PHP 8.2.0 to 8.2.35, 8.3.0 to 8.3.36, 8.4.0 to 8.4.27 and 8.5.0 to 8.5.12 (some CVEs affect only some branches)

Fixed versions

8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13; PHP 8.6.0 includes the fixes

Exposure

Internet-facing PHP applications; exploitability depends on configuration and on the application

Workaround

Set session.upload_progress.enabled = 0 (CVE-2026-115560); disable FastCGI connection reuse on the front end (CVE-2026-129289); other CVEs have their own workarounds

Exploitation

No known in-the-wild exploitation; a public proof of concept exists for CVE-2026-115560 in a lab setup

What is CVE-2026-115560?

CVE-2026-115560 is a flaw in PHP’s session upload progress feature. When a client uploads a file, PHP writes the upload’s progress into the user’s session, including a value the client controls. PHP supports several session serialization formats, and if that data is written in one format (php_serialize or php_binary) and later read in another (php), the reader can treat attacker-supplied bytes as serialized object data.

This can happen when an application switches session.serialize_handler at runtime before calling session_start(), or when separate applications, PHP-FPM pools, virtual hosts or command-line jobs with different settings share the same session storage. If the reading application has a suitable deserialization gadget chain, the attacker can execute code with the privileges of the PHP worker. According to the PHP advisory, the original report demonstrated command execution with a Guzzle gadget on PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12, and with a Monolog gadget.

The fix turns session upload progress off by default and blocks runtime changes to session settings while the feature is enabled. An explicit session.upload_progress.enabled = 1 in existing configuration still overrides the new default, and the PHP project notes that matching serializers across separate configurations is still the administrator’s responsibility.

What is CVE-2026-129289?

CVE-2026-129289 is an HTTP request smuggling flaw in PHP-FPM. When an application opens php://input but does not read the request body to the end, PHP can leave the unread bytes on a persistent FastCGI connection. An attacker can place a crafted FastCGI message in that body, and PHP-FPM accepts it as a new request that the web server never created or authorized.

The forged request controls FastCGI parameters, including the script to run and administrator-level PHP settings, which lets the attacker execute attacker-controlled PHP code as the worker in a single unauthenticated request, provided they know the path of an existing PHP script on the server. According to the PHP advisory, no non-default PHP setting, memory corruption or race condition is needed, and the bug has existed since PHP 5.6.0.

Exploitation requires a front end that reuses backend connections, such as nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on, or HAProxy FastCGI applications that keep connections open. Standard nginx and Apache configurations that close the FastCGI connection after each request are not affected by the demonstrated attack. LSAPI is affected by the same cleanup bug, but the advisory does not establish code execution through LSAPI.

Which PHP versions are affected?

PHP branch

Affected versions

Fixed version

8.5

8.5.0 to 8.5.12

8.5.13

8.4

8.4.0 to 8.4.27

8.4.28

8.3

8.3.0 to 8.3.36

8.3.37

8.2

8.2.0 to 8.2.35

8.2.36

8.6

Not listed as affected

8.6.0 (released with the fixes)

These ranges apply to CVE-2026-115560, CVE-2026-129289 and most of the other vulnerabilities in the release; a few affect only some branches (see below). PHP 8.1 and older are end of life and received no release, although the PHP project notes that older versions may also be affected (session upload progress was introduced in PHP 5.4.0). Linux distributions often backport fixes without changing the PHP version number, so check your distribution’s security tracker as well as the version string. PHP bundled in container images and application platforms needs its own update.

Additional vulnerabilities fixed in the same release

The other five critical vulnerabilities (all CVSS 4.0 9.2 according to the PHP project):

CVE-2026-126714 (8.2 to 8.5): partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution. Requires attacker influence over session data, an interrupted write and a gadget chain. Disabling session upload progress removes one input path but is not a full fix.

CVE-2026-129496 (8.2 to 8.5): a timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution. Requires a startup diagnostic and PHP error logging to a file; code execution was demonstrated locally in PHP-FPM and Apache mod_php under additional assumptions.

CVE-2026-129481 (8.3 to 8.5): use-after-free after an interrupted session shutdown. Code execution has not been demonstrated. Disabling session upload progress does not address it.

CVE-2026-129474 (8.5 only): use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution, confirmed by the PHP project on PHP 8.5. It depends on the application and requires bypassing address randomization.

CVE-2026-129182 (8.5 only): use-after-free in the fatal error backtrace after shutdown. Code execution through this path has not been demonstrated.

The release also fixes four high-severity issues: a PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free that allows local privilege escalation to root when the FPM master runs as root (CVE-2026-129291, affecting configurations with catch_workers_output enabled, including the official PHP-FPM Docker images), a denial of service through folded HTTP response headers (CVE-2026-127960), mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs that can send data in plaintext (CVE-2026-128064), and a PHAR signature bypass (CVE-2026-128090). Six medium-severity issues affect PHP-CGI, SOAP, DOM, the URI extension and the PHP-FPM status page.

Is there a patch for CVE-2026-115560 and CVE-2026-129289?

Yes. PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 and 8.5.13 were released on November 19, 2026 and are available on the PHP downloads page. PHP 8.6.0, released the same day, includes the same fixes. Linux distributions, container image maintainers and hosting platforms that ship PHP need to release their own updated packages.

How to mitigate the PHP vulnerabilities

The best fix is to upgrade to the fixed release for your branch. Each critical vulnerability has a different workaround, and no single setting covers all of them.

Inventory: find every PHP installation, including PHP in container images, PHP-FPM pools and application platforms, and note which ones run PHP-FPM behind nginx, Apache or HAProxy.

Upgrade: move to PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13 or 8.6.0, then restart the PHP master process and all workers.

CVE-2026-115560: set session.upload_progress.enabled = 0 in php.ini or the FPM pool configuration. Calling ini_set() from the application is too late. Check for explicit settings that re-enable it, even after upgrading.

CVE-2026-129289: disable FastCGI connection reuse: leave nginx fastcgi_keep_conn off, leave Apache enablereuse off, or configure other front ends to close the backend connection after each request. Never expose PHP-FPM listeners to untrusted networks.

CVE-2026-129474 and CVE-2026-129182 (PHP 8.5): set zend.exception_ignore_args = 1 or fatal_error_backtraces = 0.

CVE-2026-129496: fix configuration errors that produce startup warnings, or send PHP errors to syslog instead of a log file.

CVE-2026-129291: disable catch_workers_output in affected FPM pools, and avoid running the FPM master as root where possible.

Prioritize internet-facing PHP-FPM servers behind connection-reusing front ends, and applications that share session storage or change session settings at runtime.

Is CVE-2026-115560 being exploited in the wild?

There are no known reports of in-the-wild exploitation of any of the vulnerabilities, and none is listed in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. A public proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-115560 has been available on GitHub since October, but it targets a deliberately vulnerable lab application with a built-in gadget. With full technical details for all 17 vulnerabilities now public, especially for the PHP-FPM request smuggling flaw, exploit attempts are likely to follow.

How can Orca help?

Orca enables customers to quickly identify assets running vulnerable PHP versions, including PHP installed from OS packages and PHP bundled in container images, and to understand their exposure in context, including internet accessibility, runtime reachability and asset criticality, so they can prioritize remediation based on real risk rather than CVSS alone.

Title: PHP Patches Seven Critical RCE Vulnerabilities
Context: Residing in the session upload progress feature, it could be triggered to write attacker data using one session serialization format and then read it using another
Full Text:
PHP on Thursday rolled out a fresh set of security patches as part of its four-week update schedule, including fixes for seven critical-severity remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities.

First in line is CVE-2026-115560, which was publicly disclosed last month, two days after PHP2Shell patches landed. Residing in the session upload progress feature, it could be triggered to write attacker data using one session serialization format and then read it using another.

“A mismatched decoder can interpret part of a session key as serialized object data. An application with a suitable object gadget chain can then execute code with the privileges of the PHP worker,” PHP’s advisory reads.

Next in line is CVE-2026-129481, described as a use-after-free that occurs after a session shutdown has been interrupted, and which PHP describes as an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-109619, one of the two PHP2Shell flaws fixed in October and now widely exploited.

“An attacker who can cause an application’s session cleanup to fail in this way may corrupt memory or crash a reused PHP worker. The use-after-free could potentially lead to remote code execution, but code execution through this specific field has not been demonstrated,” PHP notes, adding that PHP 8.2 is not affected.

Another use-after-free, CVE-2026-129182, covers additional exploitation scenarios for CVE-2026-109619, an RCE via stale global state. According to PHP, however, RCE via these scenarios has not been demonstrated.

Impacting PHP 8.5 and later, CVE-2026-129474 is a use-after-free weakness that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a fatal error and achieve RCE. “Exploitation depends on the application and requires control over enough request data to influence memory allocation, a reachable magic method call, and a fatal error at the relevant point,” PHP says.

Attackers able to influence session contents and interrupt the write of serialized data to a session file may trigger the deserialization of attacker-controlled content when the session is next opened. Tracked as CVE-2026-126714, the flaw could lead to RCE via a suitable object gadget chain in the application.

PHP also patched CVE-2026-129289, a PHP-FPM request smuggling issue caused by PHP reading a request-body stream lazily, treating a request body as handled during request shutdown and skipping the normal cleanup that discards unread input.

“PHP can fail to discard unread bytes from an HTTP request body before reusing a persistent PHP-FPM or LSAPI connection. In PHP-FPM, an unauthenticated attacker can make those bytes form a separate FastCGI request, bypass front-end routing and execute attacker-controlled PHP code with the privileges of the worker,” PHP explains.

The seventh critical-severity vulnerability patched today, CVE-2026-129496, resides in the timezone cache. PHP can retain a reference to it when writing a diagnostic to a PHP error log file during process startup, and a later diagnostic can access the freed cache before it is reset.

“On affected configurations, a remote attacker can trigger memory corruption, cause a worker to crash, and potentially execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the PHP worker,” PHP explains.

PHP 8.6.0 and PHP 8.5.13 were rolled out with fixes for all critical bugs and for 10 high and medium-severity flaws. Patches for most issues were also included in PHP 8.4.28, PHP 8.3.37, and PHP 8.2.36. More information is available on PHP’s news archive page.

Title: CyberPower PowerPanel Exploited to Run Malicious Code on Domain Controller
Context: An attacker has abused CyberPower's PowerPanel Business (PBB) software to run malicious scripts on a domain controller, the server that controls logins across a Windows network,...
Full Text:
An attacker has abused CyberPower's PowerPanel Business (PBB) software to run malicious scripts on a domain controller, the server that controls logins across a Windows network, turning a power management feature into a remote command channel.

Symantec detailed the intrusion in research published November 18. PowerPanel Business manages uninterruptible power supply (UPS) battery backups. Because organizations rely on it to shut servers down safely in an outage, it often runs on important systems such as hypervisors and database and file servers.

How the UPS Software Was Abused

Administrators can configure PPB to launch a script when it detects a power problem, and its service executes that script with SYSTEM privileges, the highest level in Windows. Symantec said this meant the attacker could run code without a software bug and without setting up a service or scheduled task.

According to Symantec, the attacker uploaded scripts through the web console, then used them to stage an antivirus killer and copy the Active Directory database, which stores credentials for every account on the network. A persistent implant followed, loaded through DLL sideloading, in which a legitimate program is tricked into loading a malicious library.

The attacker leaned mostly on tools that ship with Windows, and the data collection scripts were rewritten several times during the intrusion. Symantec read that trial and error as a sign of a human operator working live.

Read more on management software attacks: Chinese State Actor Used AI to Compromise ConnectWise Tenants

What Defenders Should Check

Symantec did not say how the attacker got into the network or onto the PPB console. Possible routes to the console, it said, included stolen administrator credentials and previously disclosed weaknesses in the product, such as a default administrator password, hard-coded credentials and a file upload flaw.

Symantec said the feature "simply accepts a script, stores it, and runs it as SYSTEM." Since PPB often sits on the machines an attacker would prize most, it urged organizations to treat power-management software with the same suspicion as remote administration tools.

Its advice included limiting console access to specific administrator machines, keeping the console off the internet, replacing the default administrator password and staying patched. It also told organizations to check the folders PPB runs scripts from, assume any unfamiliar script is malicious, reset Active Directory credentials if indicators turned up and protect power-management hosts as high-value systems.

Symantec did not identify the victim or link the activity to any known group. With no data theft or ransomware seen, it said the attackers' motives remained unclear.

Title: PHP Releases Patches to Fix 18 Vulnerabilities
Context: The PHP Foundation has released security patches for a new set of 18 vulnerabilities, seven of which are marked critical
Full Text:
The PHP Foundation has released security patches for a new set of 18 vulnerabilities, seven of which are marked critical.

These vulnerabilities affect all supported PHP versions but require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups to be exploited.

This set of newly disclosed PHP vulnerabilities come a month after the disclosure of two critical flaws in PHP, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and collectively known as ‘PHP2Shell.’

This was not merely a theoretical risk. In the weeks following the disclosure, security researchers began documenting real-world exploitation attempts and compromises involving internet-facing systems, demonstrating the potential consequences of leaving vulnerable PHP installations unpatched.

For example, Check Point reported campaigns exploiting PHP2Shell against its own security gateways, dating back to 30 October. The attacks involved the deployment of backdoors and even destructive tools targeting VMware ESXi virtualisation servers.

The exploitation activity also extended to Palo Alto Networks firewalls, with attackers targeting devices whose administrative interfaces were exposed to the internet.

Of the flaws published in the November update one is a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in session upload progress, tracked as CVE-2026-115560. It was disclosed by PHP on October 23, two days after PHP released emergency fixes for the critical PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. It has been noted that exploitation of this vulnerability requires a highly specific and unlikely combination of conditions.

PHP Session Handling Flaws Enable Remote Code Execution

One of the new critical flaws, dubbed ‘PHPAfterShell’ and tracked as CVE-2026-126714, was discovered by security firm Depthfirst using AI frontier models tuned for cybersecurity tasks.

The vulnerability lives in PHP’s session handling with file-based storage, the default (session.save_handler = files).

By exploiting a flaw in this process, an attacker can manipulate a session while a file is being uploaded, potentially tricking the server into executing arbitrary code.

Successful exploitation could allow a remote attacker access to sensitive information, including login credentials and customer records, modify session data, spy on visitors or disrupt the affected service.

It affects the following versions:

PHP 8.5 < 8.5.13

PHP 8.4 < 8.4.28

PHP 8.3 < 8.3.37

PHP 8.2 < 8.2.36

PHP 8.1 and earlier are end-of-life

PHP Security Patches Address 16 Additional Vulnerabilities

The other vulnerabilities addressed in PHP’s 19 November 2026 security release include the following:

CVE-2026-129481 (CVSS 9.2): A use-after-free vulnerability triggered by an interrupted session shutdown, potentially allowing memory corruption and remote code execution

CVE-2026-129474 (CVSS 9.2): A use-after-free flaw in magic method backtraces that could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code

CVE-2026-129182 (CVSS 9.2): A use-after-free vulnerability involving the repopulation of the last fatal error backtrace after shutdown, potentially leading to remote code execution

CVE-2026-129496 (CVSS 9.2): A use-after-free vulnerability in the time zone cache that could potentially lead to remote code execution

CVE-2026-129501 (CVSS 6.3): A double-free vulnerability during DOM XML serialization that can cause memory corruption and denial of service

CVE-2026-129538 (CVSS 6.9): An out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in PHP-CGI when correcting the PATH_INFO environment variable, potentially resulting in memory corruption

CVE-2026-129291 (CVSS 8.8): A use-after-free vulnerability in PHP-FPM's epoll event handling that could allow local privilege escalation

CVE-2026-129289 (CVSS 9.2): A request-smuggling vulnerability caused by unread HTTP request bodies, potentially allowing attackers to manipulate how requests are processed

CVE-2026-129292 (CVSS 5.3): A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the PHP-FPM status endpoint, caused by insufficient escaping of user and script fields

CVE-2026-128090 (CVSS 7.7): An OpenSSL signature verification bypass caused by an algorithm downgrade, potentially allowing malicious PHAR archives to pass signature checks

CVE-2026-15353 (CVSS 6.3): An information disclosure vulnerability involving malformed array dimensions during SOAP processing

CVE-2026-129506 (CVSS 6.3): A use-after-free vulnerability when processing DTD entity references, potentially resulting in memory corruption

CVE-2026-128064 (CVSS 8.2): A vulnerability involving mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs that could cause sensitive information to be transmitted in plaintext rather than encrypted

CVE-2026-127960 (CVSS 8.7): A denial-of-service vulnerability involving folded HTTP response headers, potentially allowing attackers to disrupt service availability

CVE-2026-129438 (CVSS 6.3): An incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization vulnerability affecting oversized input, potentially resulting in invalid URI output

CVE-2026-48841 (CVSS not published): a vulnerability in the bundled uriparser library (a PHP third-party dependency) addressed by upgrading the dependency to version 1.0.3

PHP Ecosystem Projects Prepare Security Updates

The patches, published on November 19, are part of PHP’s regular four-week release cycle and come alongside the release of several versions of PHP (8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13 and 8.6).

The PHP team warned users about the vulnerabilities and their forthcoming fixes on November 18.

Users are strongly encouraged to prepare to upgrade promptly once the releases become available. Technical details and fixed version numbers will be published alongside the releases.

Maintainers of open-source projects that rely on PHP have already been working to incorporate the security fixes into their software and distributions, helping ensure that patches reach downstream users as quickly as possible.

For instance, Kevin Dunglas, creator of FrankenPHP, a modern PHP application server built around the Caddy web server, said on X that the project is working with The PHP Foundation and Docker to provide updated builds as soon as the patched PHP version becomes available. These will include static binaries, RPM and DEB packages, Homebrew packages and Docker images based on Debian and Alpine Linux.

Meanwhile, Laravel, a popular open-source PHP framework used by developers to build websites, web applications and APIs, said on X it was already working on a remediation plan to protect applications running across its hosting and deployment services.

Title: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
Context: The PHP Foundation has released security updates to address multiple critical security flaws that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution on affected deployments,...
Full Text:
The PHP Foundation has released security updates to address multiple critical security flaws that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution on affected deployments, including CVE-2026-115560.

The list of vulnerabilities is as follows -

CVE-2026-115560 (CVSS score: 9.2) - An improper input validation vulnerability that could result in remote code execution, file modification, session corruption, or denial-of-service. (Fixed in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, 8.6.0)

CVE-2026-129182 (CVSS score: 9.2) - A use-after-free vulnerability that could result in memory corruption and possible full remote code execution, as in the case of CVE-2026-109619. (Fixed in PHP 8.5.13, 8.6.0)

CVE-2026-126714 (CVSS score: 9.2) - A Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerability that could result in the execution of arbitrary code with the privileges of the PHP worker. Successful exploitation requires an attacker's influence over the session data, an interruption at a useful point in the write, and an application with a suitable deserialization gadget chain. (Fixed in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, 8.6.0)

CVE-2026-129289 (CVSS score: 9.2) - An inconsistent interpretation of HTTP requests vulnerability that could result in execution of attacker-controlled PHP code as the worker without another user's interaction or a non-default PHP configuration. Successful exploitation requires a front end that enables persistent backend connections and an application path that opens "php://input" without reading it fully, such as nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on, HAProxy FastCGI applications that retain backend connections, and LSAPI. (Fixed in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, 8.6.0)

CVE-2026-129474 (CVSS score: 9.2) - A use-after-free vulnerability that could result in remote code execution on PHP 8.5 and later. Successful exploitation depends on the application and requires control over enough request data to influence memory allocation, a reachable magic method call, and a fatal error at the relevant point. (Fixed in PHP 8.5.13, 8.6.0)

CVE-2026-129481 (CVSS score: 9.2) - A use-after-free vulnerability that could cause an application's session cleanup to fail and potentially corrupt memory, crash a reused PHP worker, or potentially allow remote code execution. (Fixed in PHP 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, 8.6.0)

CVE-2026-129496 (CVSS score: 9.2) - A use-after-free vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code with their privileges on an affected deployment. (Fixed in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, 8.6.0)

CVE-2026-129291 (CVSS score: 8.8) - A use-after-free vulnerability that could result in local privilege escalation. Successful exploitation requires local code execution in an FPM worker, an affected pool with catch_workers_output enabled, the epoll event backend, and the ability to manipulate worker lifetimes and retain inherited pipe descriptors. (Fixed in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13, 8.6.0)

Depthfirst, which has codenamed CVE-2026-126714 "phpAfterShell," has described it as a critical flaw that can enable a remote attacker to run arbitrary code on affected servers.

"If a pwrite()/ftruncate() update is interrupted, PHP may leave behind a malformed session file that is later loaded by session_start(), yielding an arbitrary deserialization primitive," Depthfirst said. "Chained with another of our PHP-native deserialization-to-RCE findings, this leads directly to remote code execution."

It affects any application that runs an affected PHP version with file-based sessions. If immediate patching is not possible, it's advised to turn off session upload progress.

Patches for the flaws are available in the following versions -

PHP 8.2.36

PHP 8.3.37

PHP 8.4.28

PHP 8.5.13

PHP 8.6.0

Users who are using existing 8.2.x, 8.3.x, 8.4.x, and 8.5.x versions of PHP are advised to update to the latest version for optimal protection.

Title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaw (CVSS 9.8) Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
Context: A critical flaw in VMware vCenter lets an attacker with network access bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system, Broadcom, which owns VMware, said in an...
Full Text:
A critical flaw in VMware vCenter lets an attacker with network access bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system, Broadcom, which owns VMware, said in an advisory published today.

Fixed versions are out for all supported branches, and the company lists no workaround. vCenter is the central console for managing an organization's ESX hosts and virtual machines.

The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-123890 and is rated 9.8 on the CVSS scoring system. "VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service," the advisory says.

In an FAQ published with the advisory, the company says the issue "qualifies under ITIL methodologies as an emergency change," and urges organizations to consult their security staff immediately on timing.

The company has not reported any attacks exploiting the flaw, or any public exploit code. It also does not say what level of access an attacker gains after the bypass. Credit for reporting the bug goes to Google-owned Mandiant.

The bug is present in vCenter 8.0, 9.0, and 9.1, and in the vCenter builds that ship inside VMware Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, and the Telco Cloud Platform and Telco Cloud Infrastructure products. That includes the older Cloud Foundation 5.x line. It is there whether or not Enhanced Linked Mode is in use.

Older versions are not cleared. The company no longer evaluates versions past end of support, and says vSphere 6.5 and 6.7 should be presumed affected. The same goes for vSphere 7.0, which left general support in October 2025, and whose customers can request a patch under an extended support contract.

None of the five flaws in the advisory lets code run on an ESX host from inside a virtual machine, and ESX itself is not affected, the advisory FAQ says.

There is no fallback for systems that cannot be updated yet: asked whether a workaround exists, the FAQ answers "Not as listed by Broadcom," while noting that mitigations may still exist in an organization's own defenses.

The updates are cumulative and cannot be installed through vCenter Quick Patch. Virtual machines continue running while vCenter installs the update, though management access drops briefly, and some encryption operations against a Standard Key Provider become unavailable until vCenter is back online.

One warning applies to upgrades already in progress: installing vCenter 8.0 U3m or 9.0.2.0200 blocks a later upgrade to VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.1, a conflict the FAQ calls a "Back-in-Time" issue. The options are to upgrade vCenter to 9.1.1 first and apply the security update there, or to wait briefly for VCF 9.1.2.

The bypass is the second critical authentication flaw in the VMware Directory Service this year. The earlier vCenter flaws, patched on July 29, included CVE-2026-59309, another 9.8-rated bypass in the same component per the July advisory, alongside a directory-traversal bug, CVE-2026-59310.

Attacks on that traversal flaw began five days after its disclosure, German incident response firm QUIRSO assessed in August, linking them with moderate confidence to a suspected China-nexus actor.

The August attacks compromised an estimated 361 IP addresses in 47 countries and deployed Babuk-derived ransomware on ESXi hosts. Broadcom has reported no attacks on the new bypass.

The advisory also fixes four lower-severity flaws, rated 6.7 to 8.1: a SQL injection (CVE-2026-123891) and a command injection (CVE-2026-123892) in SDDC Manager, a privilege escalation to root on the SDDC Manager appliance (CVE-2026-123893), and a SAML token signature bypass in VMware Tools for Windows (CVE-2026-123894), exploitable only where Guest Alias mapping is configured. Each needs an authenticated or already privileged actor, and the last one stays inside the guest virtual machine.

Title: Critical NGINX ‘NGINX2Root’ bugs let attackers hijack servers
Context: Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities dubbed "nginx2root" allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers, with researchers demonstrating how the...
Full Text:
Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities dubbed "nginx2root" allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers, with researchers demonstrating how the flaws can be chained with a Linux kernel bug to gain root access.

The two HTTP/2 vulnerabilities were discovered independently by researchers at Xint, Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, and Rapid7, while Xint also discovered three additional NGINX RCE flaws.

Censys later reproduced the underlying memory corruption conditions in four of the five flaws through lab testing, but did not achieve remote code execution.

The first of the two "nginx2root" flaws is CVE-2026-123007, a flow-control bug that can corrupt memory in an NGINX worker. It impacts all versions from 1.31.8 down to 1.9.5, released in 2015.

Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated remote code execution on a server hosting ordinary static files over HTTP/2 with TLS, while Xint demoed root access by chaining it with a separate Linux kernel flaw.

Xint says the separate vulnerability affects the Linux kernel's SCTP subsystem and can be used to escape an NGINX Docker container and gain root privileges on the underlying host.

The second flaw is CVE-2026-123633, a use-after-free problem that affects NGINX when it accepts HTTP/2 connections and proxies requests to a backend. It impacts all versions from 1.19.7 through 1.31.8.

When the worker runs low on connection slots, it can close an active connection and free memory that a request still uses. Wiz also demonstrated remote code execution via CVE-2026-123633, but the firm is not publicly releasing its proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits at this time.

The other three flaws the researchers discovered and F5 fixed are CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123634, and CVE-2026-113425, all use-after-free vulnerabilities affecting HTTP/3 reverse proxying, DNS resolution with subrequests, and mail proxy authentication, respectively.

The flaws were fixed in NGINX Open Source 1.30.7 stable and 1.31.9 mainline. NGINX Plus users should update to versions 37.0.8.1 or 37.3.0.1.

F5’s latest security update also addresses five more vulnerabilities not highlighted in the Wiz or Xint reports.

The most notable is CVE-2026-118899, a high-severity issue that allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a worker to enter an infinite loop while reading a request body over TLS 1.3, resulting in denial of service.

For system administrators, it is recommended to upgrade immediately to the latest NGINX release, or temporarily disable HTTP/2 until an upgrade is possible. However, this mitigation only covers the two "nginx2root" flaws.

Evaluating the risk

Regarding the real exploitability risk of "nginx2root," security researcher Florian Roth says it's worse than Node2Shell and Java2Shell, but doesn’t appear to be an imminent threat for most NGINX deployments.

Commenting on X, Roth said the flaws are exploitable in non-default configurations, warning that claims of widespread exposure based solely on NGINX version numbers are misleading.

Xint previously reported that 98.9% of NGINX hosts disclosing recognizable versions were running software within the affected range, but this does not account for whether HTTP/2 is enabled or security fixes have been backported.

The two HTTP/2 flaws require an unpatched server with HTTP/2 enabled on a listener an attacker can reach, while CVE-2026-123633 also requires NGINX to proxy requests to a backend.

Roth scanned a sample of a few hundred NGINX HTTPS endpoints from Shodan and found that roughly 66% of them support HTTP/2, but confirming actual exposure requires checking the server’s configuration and whether a fix has been backported.

According to Censys' live exposure tracker, approximately 8.8 million NGINX services were potentially exposed to CVE-2026-123007 as of November 19, based on affected version numbers and HTTP/2 support.

The company reports that more than 511,000 previously exposed services have already been patched or mitigated, while another 104 million NGINX services do not disclose their versions, making it difficult to determine whether they are affected.

Title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw That Could Give Unauthenticated Attackers Control of Sites
Context: Under specific conditions, a critical vulnerability in Drupal core can allow an attacker without login credentials to use the built-in installer to attempt to reinstall a site
Full Text:
Under specific conditions, a critical vulnerability in Drupal core can allow an attacker without login credentials to use the built-in installer to attempt to reinstall a site.

That can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution, and the project rates the vulnerable configurations as uncommon. Fixed releases for all supported branches shipped yesterday.

The Drupal Security Team disclosed the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-132165, yesterday and rated it critical, 18 out of 25 on the project's risk scale.

The installer ships in every copy of Drupal core as the file /core/install.php and stays on the site after installation. Core's default .htaccess rules do not block requests to it, so blocking it is left to each site.

No attacks are reported in the security advisory, which rates exploitation as complex and records an existing proof-of-concept exploit. Some exploit paths are blocked where the web server cannot write to or change permissions on settings.php.

The team had told site owners in an advance notice earlier this week to set aside time for the update, warning that exploits may be developed within hours or days.

Every release below 10.6.22 is affected, along with Drupal 11 releases from 11.0.0 before 11.3.22 and from 11.4.0 before 11.4.13.

What to Do Now

The fixed versions, detailed in the project's release notes, are:

Drupal 11.4.x: update to 11.4.13

Drupal 11.3.x: update to 11.3.22

Drupal 10.6.x: update to 10.6.22

The team recommends blocking the installer even after updating. Sites that cannot update yet should follow the project's installer guidance, updated yesterday, which describes three options: a deny rule in the web server configuration, an .htaccess rule, or removing the file and keeping it removed with Composer scripts.

Sites that use the Drupal Steward protection service are already protected from known attack vectors, according to the team, and should still update in case new vectors emerge.

Drupal 11.2.x and earlier, 10.5.x and earlier, and Drupal 8 and 9 are end-of-life and get no fix. The 11.3.x branch and Drupal 10 lose security coverage altogether in December under the project's support schedule.

In the week of November 8, 154,485 of the 528,430 sites reporting usage data to drupal.org, about 29 percent, were running end-of-life branches.

The flaw was found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, an automated service the AI company launched on October 8 to look for vulnerabilities in open-source projects that opt in. Findings go to maintainers without human review, each with a reproducer and, where available, a candidate patch, according to its launch announcement.

Drupal's security team said on November 2 that a surge of security reports, which it attributes to AI tools, is more than it can sustain at its current funding, and that it is cutting security coverage for core minor versions from 12 months to 8 starting in 2027.

This is the second critical remote code execution flaw fixed in Drupal core in two months, after the Field UI flaw patched on October 14, which also had at least one exploit path that needed no login.

Title: ARMORY CASTLE Exploits vSphere
Context: ARMORY CASTLE exploited a zero-day vulnerability to gain access to the VMware server, and likely used an additional set of malware customized to this environment to conduct...
Full Text:
Written by: Jayson Frost, Bryce Greathouse, Dhanesh Kizhakkinan, John Palmisano, Steve Rasch, Daniel Sislo, John Wolfram Introduction On Oct. 15, 2026, Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) published a blog post detailing recent activity in which the suspected PRC-nexus threat actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly tracked as UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-102764, a zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support, which was patched in BT26-05. We also described some of the threat actor’s post-exploitation operations. In this blog we describe additional post-compromise activity involving the exploitation of a vulnerability in VMware vCenter and the deployment of additional malware families. On Nov. 19, 2026, VMware disclosed CVE-2026-123890, which impacts VMware vCenter Server deployments. vSphere consists of both ESXi (the hypervisor) and vCenter Server. The vCenter server is a centralized platform deployed as a Photon Linux virtual appliance and is used to configure, control, and monitor ESXi host environments. CVE-2026-123890 is an unauthenticated Secure Remote Password (SRP-6a) session key disclosure vulnerability over Distributed Computing Environment/Remote Procedure Calls (DCE/RPC). Successful exploitation results in a remote authentication bypass which creates an authenticated session established as administrator@vsphere.local. Using the authenticated administrator session, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands and acquire files, including the data.mdb database, by leveraging the vCenter Server Directory Service (vmdird) RPC interface vmdirdbcp. We strongly recommend that affected organizations immediately apply the security patches provided by Broadcom to remediate the vulnerability. ARMORY CASTLE exploited this vulnerability in early September 2026 using BONESAW, according to forensic evidence. BONESAW is a utility primarily built to facilitate remote exploitation written in Golang , which utilizes CVE-2026-123890 to exfiltrate the arbitrary Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (LMDB), hijack the SAML Security Token Service (STS), and create a Single Sign On (SSO) Administrator account. ARMORY CASTLE’s use of BONESAW represents significant new insight into this threat actor’s post-exploitation tactics. In this campaign, ARMORY CASTLE exploited two zero-days, and deployed three sets of malware specifically tailored for operating on targeted devices, indicating deep platform expertise and substantial resource backing. We are publishing this analysis, along with mitigation and hardening guidance, to support defenders in detecting this threat. Threat Detail Moving laterally from the Remote SupportRemote Support device, ARMORY CASTLE established a foothold on an internal Linux appliance, escalated privileges to root, and staged a suite of malware to support expanding access, persistence, and targeting of vCenter. BONESAW achieves full system compromise against vCenter Server 7.x and 8.x appliances through the exploitation of CVE-2026-123890. This vulnerability exploits a cryptographic logic and authorization flaw in VMware's rpc_srp_verifier service over port 2012, exposing a shared session key that can be used to create authenticated sessions as administrator@vsphere.local. BONESAW also provides the ability to stream the raw underlying LMDB file for offline parsing, extract the VMware Security Token Service (STS) SAML private RSA signing key, create a backdoor machine account via vmdir, forge administrative SAML 2.0 assertion tokens, and assign Global Administrator privileges on the vCenter root folder via the vSphere SOAP API. CVE-2026-59309 is a flaw in the vCenter Server vmdir daemon that allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker with network access to TCP ports 389 or 636 to send crafted LDAP packets with malformed authorization tokens, bypassing authentication to forge administrative sessions and create rogue Single Sign-On (SSO) accounts in the vSphere directory. Whereas CVE-2026-123890 is a flaw in the vmdir DCE/RPC interface that enables unauthenticated Secure Remote Password session key disclosure by exploiting predictable UUIDv1 timestamp generation in the SRP authentication interface, enabling the compromise of the SRP session key without knowing any passwords. Mandiant has evidence that ARMORY CASTLE had knowledge of CVE-2026-123890 prior to the disclosure of CVE-2026-59309 on July 29, 2026. This allows the threat actor to forge authentication tokens, bypass MFA, and impersonate any user. The core functionality of SAWSNAKE is a custom Go-based port of the Python-based vCenter SAML Login Tool from vcenter_saml_login.py. Mandiant also observed this TTP during BRICKSTORM intrusions conducted by suspected PRC-nexus actor UNC6201.
